name: Side By Side
label: Revelation
lede: They lasted about a year and a half, broke up before their only record came out, and that seven-song 7" has been pressed again and again for nearly four decades.

eras.title: Five months from first show to first band
eras.text: Jules Masse, a kid from Weehawken, New Jersey, saw his first hardcore show on Long Island in the early summer of 1986. Within about five months he was fronting a band out of an Alphabet City apartment, part of the youngest wave of the New York straight edge crowd.

years.h: First show: the Right Track Inn
years.p: Masse's introduction to hardcore is a Long Island bill with [[Youth of Today|9ca27db4-f127-4aeb-ae87-29e21f558c13]], [[Straight Ahead|1fd60d7c-dc35-44f5-9162-4113b6ca4a69]] and [[Sick of It All|e204ed91-3684-4561-b29b-d0b53f8459a7]].

years.h: Side By Side starts in an Alphabet City apartment
years.p: Masse, Eric Rice on guitar and Billy on bass, with Gavin borrowed from NY Hoods on drums for the early stretch.

The drummer, born in 1973, is barely into his teens. He'll go on to play in Youth of Today, [[Judge|3827fbb6-e219-4e2d-9af8-35cc9a7d8d8e]], [[Gorilla Biscuits|0320a32e-b781-40df-bf48-5cb5ee842762]] and CIV.

eras.title: On the first Rev roll call
eras.text: Revelation Records' second release gathered the new straight edge New York bands on one 7", and Side By Side were on it. They played the same bills as Youth of Today, Gorilla Biscuits and Warzone all year, then went into Don Fury's studio.

years.p: Side By Side's first appearance on record, on the label's second release. The first press was 600 black and 400 orange, the 'gold' vinyl collectors still mix up with the later yellow.

years.h: The CBGB show that got shut down
years.p: Side By Side, Youth of Today, Gorilla Biscuits and Pagan Babies on one matinee, remembered for a showdown with the club's bouncers.
The last piece of the line-up, soon to be in Gorilla Biscuits too.
The EP is cut with Fury, who also recorded Gorilla Biscuits' records. Songs like Guilty and Good Clean Fun, and a Youth Brigade cover, never got recorded.

eras.title: Gone before the record came out
eras.text: Side By Side drifted apart after the session, with no fight and no big final night planned as one. The record landed after the band was already over, and the members were already feeding the next wave of bands.

q: It wasn't poetic, it wasn't complicated... but it was genuine.
years.src: In Effect Hardcore · Wikipedia: Youth of Today
years.h: Last show: the Anthrax, and their best
years.p: The final official show is at the Connecticut club, and the band remembers it as the best they ever played.
years.xp:
There was no dramatic ending. The members simply drifted apart, and the EP was already in the can. Masse later summed up the music without any gloss.

Siegler landed in Youth of Today within months, and Brown was already playing in Gorilla Biscuits.

years.p: Out after the breakup. The first press came in two batches of 1,005 and 1,012, pressed about a week apart and identical in every way, some with one of at least three different stickers.
years.xp:
Two more 2,000-copy presses followed, and Rev's notes tell them apart by the details: silver labels with the cover opening at the bottom on the second, grey labels and a black border around the back-cover live photo on the third.

A band that never played a show behind it kept selling it anyway.

years.p: A one-off reunion at a benefit for the [[Agnostic Front|40b8a690-94e4-4c82-ad0f-73f4b841e46a]] singer.
About a year after the split, Masse starts a new band with [[Lars Weiss|c60d8790-7786-4df8-8647-7f8b2ca02c17]], who'd go on to Uppercut and Judge.

eras.title: The record that kept getting pressed
eras.text: With the band long gone, You're Only Young Once... became a Revelation evergreen. The label kept bringing it back on new colors of vinyl, and Alex Brown became a painter whose work reached MoMA.

years.p: Revelation's 12" edition: 1,109 on black vinyl and 100 on blue.
A 550-copy red vinyl press, followed by grey in 2013 and gold in 2017.
He died suddenly. By then a painter whose work is in the collection of MoMA, he is remembered through the Alex Brown Foundation, an artist residency in Des Moines, Iowa.

eras.title: Three is a magic number
eras.text: Masse, by now a lawyer in Florida, had no plans to play again. A benefit for their late guitarist brought the originals back for three shows across two continents, and they called the last one the last.

q: I never had any intention of playing with Side By Side again.
years.h: Side By Side reunite for Alex Brown
years.p: Masse, Rice, Billy and Siegler, with Weiss on second guitar, play Revolution Calling in the Netherlands in late November.
years.xp:
Weiss had played bass at the band's last show in the '80s; this time he took Brown's guitar spot. Proceeds went to the Alex Brown Foundation.

Masse was the least likely to say yes. He said the reunion came in threes, and left it at that.

years.p: A headlining benefit show in New York, thirty-five years after the record.

years.h: The last one: The Book of Revelation Records, Los Angeles
years.p: Night two of the Revelation weekend at 1720, sharing the bill with Youth of Today, billed as Side By Side's final reunion show.
